title: Do three countries make up the World count?
description: A line graph of objects launched into space has a World line and lines for the United States, China and Russia. The video adds the three countries and compares the sum with the World line in 2024. It breaks Keeko's doubt that the three lines must add up to the World.
teaching_notes: One idea: a World line counts every country, so a few country lines can add up to less than the World. Watch for students who expect the shown parts to always fill the whole.

source: In 2024 the World line is about 2850, the United States abou
video_script.why: The child can read dots on a line graph but has not yet checked whether the lines of a few countries add up to the World line.
video_script.substitution: Add the readings of the three country lines for one year, then take that sum away from the World reading.
video_script.anchor: the book's line graph of the number of objects launched into space each year
video_script.wrong_answer: the three countries make up the whole World count
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks every part of the World is drawn on the graph, so the shown parts must fill the whole.
video_script.payoff_line: about two hundred objects came from other countries

final_answer.value: No; about 200 objects come from other countries that are not shown
final_answer.spoken: no, about two hundred objects come from other countries that are not shown

never_show: the three countries add up to the World count
maths_rules: space launches in 2024: World about 2850, United States about 2250, China about 280, Russia about 120
the 200 objects come from countries whose lines the graph does not show
the book says the World count in 2024 is around 2800; the worklist reads about 2850, so the gap is about 200 either way
video_script.design: One idea: parts that are shown need not fill the whole. The wrong idea is that the shown parts always fill the whole. The space graph stays on screen; the three country readings stack into one bar beside the World bar.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>Look at the year two thousand twenty four. Do these three countries make up the World count?

<bookmark mark='cr'/>China is at about two hundred eighty, and Russia is at about one hundred twenty.

beats.on_screen: To find: do the three countries make up the World count?

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the three countries make up the whole World count, because the World is made of countries.
<bookmark mark='short'/>But the graph shows only three countries, and the bar is still short.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Every other country adds to the World line too, so their objects fill the gap.
